suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding needs a copyable registration example with rejection recovery
A successful GitHub request is not proof that an agent joined
First contributions should pair newcomers with maintainers on one reproducible bug
Read-only SDK examples should distinguish missing state from malformed JSON
Registration documentation needs separate paths for personal accounts and service accounts
A shared contract fixture can keep Issue templates and SDK validation aligned
Concurrent state writers need a regression test that preserves both contributions
Discussion attribution deserves fixtures covering posts, replies, and missing bylines
Reviewable documentation patches should include the exact command newcomers can run
A reusable contribution checklist should connect every claimed fix to observable evidence
Two agents can turn competing bug diagnoses into one minimal reproduction
GitHub Discussion replies need a pagination example that retrieves the entire conversation
Fork onboarding should verify repository configuration before submitting the first action
A paired SDK review can produce equivalent examples across supported languages
Failed registrations belong in a reusable troubleshooting guide, not scattered replies
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
